intro: This branch applies arithmetic to the physical world: measuring length, weight, volume and time, and working with shapes and angles. It covers perimeter, area and volume, and how to describe and sort shapes.

II.9.01.what: Measuring length in metric units (millimeters, centimeters, meters, kilometers) and converting between them.

levels.a: Converts between millimeters, centimeters and meters.
levels.b: Converts kilometers to meters.
levels.c: Converts meters with decimals into centimeters, as in 8.8 m is 880 cm.
levels.d: Chooses the best unit for measuring something.

II.9.02.what: Measuring length in US units (inches, feet, yards, miles) and converting between them.

levels.a: Converts between inches, feet and yards.
levels.b: Converts miles to feet.
levels.c: Converts to a mix of units, as in 81 inches is 6 feet 9 inches.
levels.d: Chooses the best unit for measuring something.

II.9.03.what: Measuring how heavy things are, in grams and kilograms or ounces and pounds.

levels.a: Converts kilograms to grams.
levels.b: Converts pounds to ounces.
levels.c: Converts decimal amounts, as in 8.6 kg is 8,600 g.
levels.d: Estimates the weight of everyday objects, like a cat.

II.9.04.what: Measuring how much a container holds, in milliliters and liters or cups, pints, quarts and gallons.

levels.a: Converts liters to milliliters.
levels.b: Converts between cups, pints, quarts and gallons.
levels.c: Converts decimal amounts, as in 8.8 liters is 8,800 milliliters.
levels.d: Estimates how much everyday containers hold, like a glass of milk.

II.9.05.what: Working with time: how long things last, converting between units, and reading timetables.

levels.a: Works out how long something lasts from its start and end times.
levels.b: Converts between hours and minutes.
levels.c: Converts between other units of time, such as days and hours.
levels.d: Reads a bus timetable to answer questions.

II.9.06.what: Finding the perimeter of a shape: the total distance around its edge.

levels.a: Counts unit lengths around a shape on a grid.
levels.b: Adds up the lengths of all the sides.
levels.c: Uses a shortcut for rectangles: twice the length plus twice the width.
levels.d: Finds a missing side when the perimeter is known.
levels.e: Works backwards from a rectangle's perimeter and a clue about its sides to find its area.
levels.f: Finds the perimeter of one strip after a square is cut into equal strips.

II.9.07.what: Finding area, the amount of flat space a shape covers, by counting squares.

levels.a: Counts whole squares to find the area of a shape on a grid.
levels.b: Counts half squares too, pairing them up to make wholes.
levels.c: Compares the areas of two shapes.
levels.d: Sees that shapes that look different can have the same area.

II.9.08.what: Finding the area of rectangles by multiplying length by width, and using this for other shapes.

levels.a: Multiplies length by width to find a rectangle's area.
levels.b: Finds a missing side when the area is known.
levels.c: Finds the area of an L-shape or similar by splitting it into rectangles.
levels.d: Solves word problems, like the area of a garden.
levels.e: Works backwards from the area and one side to find the missing side, then the perimeter.
levels.f: Finds the area of a path running around a garden, by taking the garden from the whole.

II.9.09.what: Understanding that perimeter (distance around) and area (space inside) are different, and knowing which one a job needs.

levels.a: Sees that rectangles with the same perimeter can have different areas.
levels.b: Sees that rectangles with the same area can have different perimeters.
levels.c: Decides whether a real task needs perimeter or area.
levels.d: Finds the biggest pen that can be enclosed with a given length of fence.
levels.e: Finds a rectangle's sides when both its area and perimeter are given.
levels.f: Counts every whole-number rectangle with a given perimeter whose area is above a target.

II.9.10.what: Finding volume, the amount of space a solid takes up, by counting unit cubes.

levels.a: Counts the unit cubes in a solid.
levels.b: Counts the cubes in one layer, then multiplies by the number of layers.
levels.c: Compares which of two boxes is made of more cubes.
levels.d: Picks out a box built from an exact number of cubes.

II.9.11.what: Finding the volume of a box by multiplying length, width and height.

levels.a: Multiplies length times width times height.
levels.b: Uses the area of the base times the height, including finding a missing height.
levels.c: Finds the volume of a solid made of two boxes by adding them.
levels.d: Solves word problems, like the volume of a fish tank.
levels.e: Works out how many small cubes fit exactly inside a box.
levels.f: Solves the painted-cube puzzle: how many small cubes have paint on exactly one or two faces.

II.9.12.what: Learning the basic words of geometry: points, lines, segments and rays, and how lines can meet.

levels.a: Tells apart a point, a line (endless both ways) and a segment (with two ends).
levels.b: Recognizes a ray: a line with one end that goes on forever the other way.
levels.c: Recognizes parallel lines, which never meet.
levels.d: Recognizes perpendicular lines, which meet at a square corner.

II.9.13.what: Understanding angles as an amount of turn, measured in degrees, and naming the different kinds.

levels.a: Knows a full turn is 360 degrees.
levels.b: Sorts angles as right (a square corner), acute (smaller) or obtuse (bigger).
levels.c: Knows a straight angle is a half turn, and two make a full turn.
levels.d: Names an angle using three letters, with the corner in the middle.

II.9.14.what: Using a protractor, a half-circle measuring tool, to measure and draw angles.

levels.a: Chooses which of the protractor's two scales to read.
levels.b: Measures an angle with a protractor.
levels.c: Draws an angle of a given size with a protractor.
levels.d: Estimates the size of an angle before measuring.

II.9.15.what: Adding angles together and finding missing angles.

levels.a: Adds two angles side by side to find the whole angle.
levels.b: Finds a missing part of a known angle, such as a right angle.
levels.c: Uses the fact that angles all the way around a point add to 360 degrees.
levels.d: Solves word problems, like how far a door has swung open.
levels.e: Splits a straight or right angle into two parts when one is several times the other.
levels.f: Finds the angle between a clock's hands at a given time, allowing for the hour hand's drift.

II.9.16.what: Sorting triangles by their sides and by their angles.

levels.a: Names triangles by their sides: all equal, two equal, or none equal.
levels.b: Names triangles by their angles: all acute, one right angle, or one obtuse angle.
levels.c: Names a triangle by both its sides and its angles.
levels.d: Decides whether a given kind of triangle can exist.

II.9.17.what: Sorting four-sided shapes (quadrilaterals) and seeing how their families fit together.

levels.a: Names squares, rectangles and rhombuses (four equal sides).
levels.b: Names parallelograms (two pairs of parallel sides) and trapezoids (exactly one pair).
levels.c: Places shapes in a family tree, seeing a square as a special rectangle.
levels.d: Judges statements like every square is a rhombus as true or false.

II.9.18.what: Finding lines of symmetry: fold lines where one half of a shape matches the other exactly.

levels.a: Picks which line is a line of symmetry.
levels.b: Counts how many lines of symmetry a shape has.
levels.c: Completes a shape on a grid so it has a given line of symmetry.
levels.d: Recognizes shapes that have no line of symmetry.

II.9.19.what: Locating points on a grid using two numbers (coordinates): how far across, then how far up.

levels.a: Knows the two axes and the starting corner, and reads points on an axis.
levels.b: Finds the point with given coordinates.
levels.c: Reads the coordinates of a point.
levels.d: Spots a pattern in a set of points and predicts the next one.

II.9.20.what: Solving word problems that bring together measurement, perimeter, area and volume.

levels.a: Solves problems that need converting units, like meters and centimeters.
levels.b: Solves problems about perimeter and area, like fencing a garden.
levels.c: Solves problems about volume, like how many liters fill a tank.
levels.d: Solves problems with several steps, like the cost of fencing with a gate.
